newsitem.title: MALTA: TRADING FALLS QUIET AT MALTA EXCHANGE.
newsitem.headline: TRADING FALLS QUIET AT MALTA EXCHANGE.

text.p: Turnover in the once weekly trading session at Malta Stock Exchange on Wednesday fell by half over the previous week, reaching 214,500 Maltese pounds ($560,000) against 500,000 pounds.
There were 93 deals, of which 42 were in equities and 51 in fixed income securities.
Equity turnover reached 50,600 pounds, with 39,658 shares changing hands. Of these, 33,741 were Bank of Valletta shares transacted in 34 deals at an average price of 124.8 cents, up eight mils.
There were five deals in Mid-Med Bank with 3,317 shares changing hands at an average price of 150.2 cents per share, up three mils.

At the same time, 1,600 Lombard Bank Malta shares were traded at an average price of 143 cents per share, unchanged. In Middle Sea Insurance, 1,000 shares sold for an average price of 121 cents each, up four mils.
In the government bond market, nine issues were dealt in, with turnover totalling just over 111,200 pounds.
Business was mainly concentrated in the 7.25 percent MGS 2006 (III) and in the 7.5 percent MGS 2011.

In the corporate bond sector, there was one deal in Mid- Med Bank 7.25 percent unsecured loan stock 2005 amounting to 1,200 pounds, seven deals in 6.5 percent Gasan Bonds 1998/99 at 10,862 pounds and four deals in the 8.25 percent Suncrest Bonds 2005/7 amounting to 40,129.40.
The share index rose to 990.32 from 987.19 the previous week.
